items.title: The parallel cap has now been exceeded on two consecutive fires - either raise it or make it binding.
items.why: policy/current.max_parallel_per_node = 1. c-0010 exceeded it deliberately for zoltarlead and recorded a deviation; this fire exceeded it for zoltarone and recorded an interpretation. Two fires running is the point at which a policy field stops constraining anything and starts documenting that it does not. The spec is genuinely ambiguous - section 3 lists max_parallel_per_node as an L3 gate, while the dispatcher runbook's section 3 names only three dispatch conditions and the cap is not among them - so this is your call, not a reading I should keep making per fire. Both exceedances are also arguably moot: no courier has ever run, so no node has ever had even one order in flight in any physical sense.
items.acceptance: policy/current carries either max_parallel_per_node raised to 2+ with a history entry, or an explicit note that the cap binds at L1 and the dispatcher must queue - after which no fire records a deviation again.

items.title: A fire that creates a task must dispatch it or name it as not-dispatched in the same fire.

Deriving from events, never from the last receipt, is the habit that caught it and is the habit to keep.
